newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end lower ahead of U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end lower ahead of U.S. holiday.

text.p: *Stocks end with modest losses as caution emerges ahead of U.S. holiday. Golds cop serious slug. Volume 327.81 million, value A$703.94, 1,198 stocks traded, 289 steady, 320 up, 589 down.
The Australian stock market chalked up modest losses by the close on Friday as caution crept in ahead of the Independence Day holiday in U.S. markets.
The All Ordinaries index lost 9.5 points to 2,733.4.
September share price index futures contracts were down 11 points at 2,767, a 33.6 point premium to the underlying index.

The market played according to script, with the light afternoon selling widely expected by traders and gold stocks taking a hammering after news that the Reserve Bank of Australia had sold 167 tonnes of gold reserves over the past six months.
This surprise sparked sharp drops in gold stocks and pushd the sector benchmark index to its lowest close since April 1993.
"Gold stocks have been the ones in the (seller's) sights today," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.
Making up 20 percent of the gold index, Normandy Mining suffered, opening nearly nine percent lower at A$1.333 before recovering ground to close 3.4 percent down at A$1.41.
Newcrest Mining slumped over six percent to A$3.20 and with Normandy topped turnover lists with over nine million shares traded in each stock.

Among others, Goldfields dived over 12 percent to A$1.66, while Acacia Resources ended 4.2 percent down at A$1.61, Emperor Mines lost over nine percent to A$1.50 and Great Central Mines lost over five percent to A$2.382.
The immediate outlook for the sector was unsettled, with traders expecting further turmoil in the precious metals sector.
"The golds and resources will become extremely volatile in the next couple of weeks, depending on what comes out," said Martin Angel of Perth-based brokerage, Eyres Reed.
The rest of the market was a mixed, patchy affair with most coming back from late morning highs as investors lightened positions in the afternoon session.
In terms of outlook, traders said with New York closed for the July 4 holiday the local market was likely to consolidate, at least early in the week, while recent rises were digested.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 24 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
Options trade was light with just 24,550 traded, while turnover in September SPI futures was a moderate 5,283 contracts.

In other local markets, Australian bonds extended their gains through the day on constant buying and closed just under fresh contract highs. With the U.S. closed Friday and nothing expected to change sentiment over the weekend, the bullish was expected to remain. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.82 percent compared to Thursday's 6.91 percent.

The Australian dollar kept calm atop 75 cents in a thin day's trade with traders reporting scant sign of follow-through selling after its offshore pullback. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the currency was keeping a grip at US$0.7519/24 having inched back from a US$0.7548 high overnight and US$0.7530/35 Thursday.
